recommendedTextbook.title: Essential Financial Accounting for Senior Secondary Schools
recommendedTextbook.author: R. A. I. Kazeem
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: NERDC & Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education

subtopics: Causes of differences between Cash Book bank balance and Bank Statement balance
Unpresented cheques, uncredited lodgements, bank charges, standing orders, direct debits
Adjusting the Cash Book (Electronic banking updates) and preparing the Bank Reconciliation Statement
objectives: Identify 6 standard causes of timing differences in bank balances
Update the Cash Book with bank charges, credit transfers, and dishonored cheques
Draft a complete Bank Reconciliation Statement reconciling adjusted cash balance with bank statement

topics.topic: Correction of Accounting Errors and the Suspense Account
subtopics: Errors that do NOT affect the agreement of the Trial Balance (Omission, commission, principle, compensation, original entry, reversal of entries)
Errors that DO affect the Trial Balance and creation of the Suspense Account
Journal entries correcting errors and eliminating the suspense balance
objectives: Differentiate errors of principle from errors of commission
Draft correcting journal entries with explanatory narrations
Open, post, and close a Suspense Account in the ledger

topics.topic: Final Accounts of a Sole Trader with Year-End Adjustments
subtopics: Trading, Profit and Loss Account (Statement of Profit or Loss)
Balance Sheet (Statement of Financial Position) horizontal and vertical formats
Year-end adjustments: Accrued expenses, prepaid expenses, bad debts written off, provision for doubtful debts
objectives: Prepare a comprehensive Trading Account showing Gross Profit calculation
Compute and record provisions for bad debts and depreciation of non-current assets
Present a classified Statement of Financial Position adhering to WAEC marking schemes

topics.topic: Control Accounts: Sales Ledger and Purchases Ledger Control
subtopics: Meaning, advantages, and sources of information for Control Accounts (Total Debtors & Total Creditors)
Sales Ledger Control Account: Debits for sales, credits for cash received, returns, discounts allowed
Purchases Ledger Control Account: Debits for cash paid, returns, discounts received, credits for purchases
objectives: Explain 3 reasons why large Nigerian enterprises maintain control accounts
Prepare Sales Ledger and Purchases Ledger Control Accounts from given transaction summaries
Identify contra-settlements (set-offs) and bad debt transfers between ledgers
